location: §4 overview, item (2): "in $\N$, not in $\R$, $V$ or a nonstandard model of $\PA$"
problem: False as a general statement and contradicts prop:univ:tv, which says (i) holds for every model of true arithmetic, including the nonstandard ones. For M ⊨ PA, M₀≅ℕ and M₀≼M iff M≡ℕ. So the step fails only in models of PA that are not elementarily equivalent to ℕ, e.g. models of PA+¬Con(PA) (Ex. A7′).
fix: Replace with: "in $\N$ and in every model of true arithmetic, but not in $\R$, in $V$, or in a model of $\PA$ that is not elementarily equivalent to $\N$ (e.g.\ a model of $\PA+\neg\Con(\PA)$, \cref{ex:univ:fail})."

location: prop:univ:learner (1): "in (N) and (dB) it also needs $\mathrm{nocap}$ whenever some free $x_i$ lies under a binder"
problem: The sentence has two errors. (a) closed(z_i) already excludes every capture instance, because closed values contain no variables; prop:univ:open(c) says so. With the closedness guard, nocap is therefore never needed in addition. (b) The condition is wrong. By prop:univ:capture(b), Cap(φ) can be empty although a free x_i lies under a binder: in (dB), or in (N) with sentences as data, e.g. φ=(x=0∧∀y(x=y)). In that case no capture guard is needed. The appendix proof correctly uses Cap(φ)≠∅.
fix: Replace with: "If parameters are admissible values, the cautious single-schema learner over $\Hk1(\FO)$ or $\Hk1(\DT)$ is sound for it only with a closedness guard. In (N) and (dB), even without parameters, it must also exclude capture instances whenever $\Cap(\varphi)\neq\emptyset$ (\cref{prop:univ:capture}(b)), by $\mathrm{nocap}$ or by $\mathrm{closed}$, which implies it; under the $\lambda$ convention this is automatic."

location: prop:univ:capture(e) "A datum at a parameter deletes $\mathrm{closed}(z_i)$ … and the accepted set becomes $\insto(\varphi)$"; tab:univ:learner row 4; app-universal proof of (e)
problem: The most-specific-guard rule deletes closed(z_i) only for the z_i whose value contains a parameter. For k≥2, the datum φ(p,0) keeps closed(z_2). The accepted set is then {φ(t1,t2): t1 capture-free, t2 closed}, which is not insto(φ).
fix: In (e): "A datum whose value at $z_i$ contains a parameter deletes $\mathrm{closed}(z_i)$ but not $\mathrm{nocap}(z_i)$; once this has happened for every $i$ (for $k=1$, after one such datum), the accepted set is $\insto(\varphi)$." In table row 4: "data with a parameter at every $z_i$ (…)". In the appendix proof of (e): "…so only $\mathrm{closed}(z_i)$ is deleted, and once it is deleted for every $i$, $\inst(\sigma_\varphi,\{\mathrm{nocap}(z_i)\}_i)$ is …".

location: prop:univ:learner (3): "It is derivable from the instances only by an $\omega$-rule (\cref{ex:univ:q})."
problem: Overstated. For many φ (logically valid ones, or over stronger theories), ∀x̄φ is first-order derivable. Ex. univ:q shows non-derivability for one φ over Q.
fix: Replace with: "\textup{(3)} In general it is not derivable from the instances in first-order logic, even over $\Q$ (\cref{ex:univ:q}); it is an $\omega$-rule step."

fix: In the overview: "Failure rates have exact formulas for one and two variables and an exponential bound in general (\cref{thm:univ:rates})." In the summary: "…two instances suffice, and the failure rates are known exactly for one and two variables."

location: \subsection sec:univ:merge, lines 200-213 (prop:univ:merge and the 'Computed (untagged u6)' paragraph)
problem: prop:univ:merge (a)-(e) restates prop:many:forall (a)-(e), with lem:many:twopoint covering (a). The u6 computation is repeated at many.tex lines 318-321. lem:univ:qf (app-universal C.6) is prop:many:qf, which many.tex lines 330-335 prove again. §4.7 also has to preview DTRC before §6 defines it.
fix: Replace lines 202-213 with: 'In the untagged setting of \cref{sec:many}, each closed instance $\varphi(t)$ can be read as its own ground target, and learning $\forall x\varphi$ then means merging instances across ``targets''. \Cref{prop:many:forall} shows that \DTRC{} does this soundly. If $\forall x\varphi$ is true, any closed instances, two with different heads, form one cluster whose only minimal template is $\sigma_\varphi$, and \DTRC{} accepts $\varphi(a)$, i.e. $\forall x\varphi$ (\cref{prop:univ:gen}). If $\forall x\varphi$ is false and an instance of $\sigma_\varphi$ is refuted, the merge is refused. With R-$\Delta_0$, ``never refuted'' means ``true'' for quantifier-free $\varphi$ (\cref{prop:many:qf}); an oracle that only evaluates closed instances certifies truth at every closed term, which in $\N$ is the $\omega$-rule and in $\R$ leaves the false $\forall x\,\neg(x\cdot x=1+1)$ unrefuted (\cref{ex:univ:fail}).' Add to prop:many:forall(e) the clause '(R-$\Delta_0$ verifies universals only by equational derivations from true closed equations; a decision procedure for RCF would refute the $\R$ example)'. Delete app-universal.tex C.6 (lines 131-153). Move the proof of prop:many:qf (many.tex 330-335) to app:many:dtrc. Editor: intro.tex l.173 cites prop:univ:merge; cite prop:many:forall instead. Saves about 0.65 pp of main text.
